page.layout: One column of running text, with a printed quotation mark (») at the start of many lines. No marginal notes, no heading. Page number and running head at the top.

main_text.p: » nim ei cauere uolo, quàm i- » pse alijs foleat.Eôdem etiam locus ille pertinet ex oratio- nè pro Plancio,unde hoc am plius intelligitur, non fine re prehensione eos fuisse,qui cũ hanc artem profesi fuissent, sufcepto tamè muneri satis- » facere non possent: Quæris, » inquit, num Iurifconsultus? » quasi quisquam fit, qui sibi » hunc falsum de iure respon- » disse dicat.omnes enim istius » modi artes in ijs reprehendũ » tur,qui cum profesi fuerint, » satisfacere non possunt: non » in ijs, qui abfuisse ab istis stu- » dijs confitentur.Perspicuum igitur esse arbitror, quod su- pe-

page.notes: The running head is too faint to read; about 12 letters, roman capitals with a numeral before them, possibly "II." followed by a title. The line "» modi artes" and the others use the printed » as a quotation mark carried over from the previous page. The mark at the bottom left ("ss..") is a faint smudge or possible gathering mark and is not transcribed. "reprehendũ" is printed with a tilde on u and continues on the next line as "tur". The page ends mid-word with "pe-", which is carried over onto the next page.
